sentences.text: Appellants are the petitioners and respondents are the respondents in the O.P. BRMR,J 3.
Learned counsel for the appellants - petitioners submits that respondent No.1 remained ex-parte before the Tribunal, hence notice is not required to him in the appeal.

4. Appellants - petitioners have filed claim petition under Sections 140(C) and 166 of the MV Act read with Rule 475/1B of APMV Rules, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.9,50,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum from the date of filing the petition till realization, for the death of Mekala Narasimhulu.

5. The learned counsel for the appellants - petitioners submits that the learned Tribunal ought to have awarded the entire amount as claimed by the appellants - petitioners, erred in taking the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month instead of taking at Rs.10,000/- per month, has not taken into consideration the future prospects of the deceased, ought to have taken the multiplier '18' instead of '16', awarded less amount under different heads and prayed to enhance the amount.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company submits that the income of the deceased taken by the Tribunal is correct, interest has to be scale down to 6% per annum and prayed to pass appropriate orders.
BRMR,J 7.
Learned counsel for the appellants - petitioners have filed calculation memo showing enhancement of compensation.
8. Appellants - petitioners have challenged the quantum in the appeal.

9. Learned Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month, deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses and arrived at Rs.4,000/- per month [6,000 - (1/3rd of 6,000 = 2,000)],
annul income comes to Rs.48,000/- [4,000 x 12], taken the age of the deceased at 33 years, applied multiplier '16' and arrived loss of dependency at Rs.7,68,000/- [48,000 x 16].
Further, learned Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards funeral and other miscellaneous expenses and awarded Rs.10,000/- towards loss of consortium.

In total learned Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.7,88,000/- with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of filing the petition till the date of deposit payable by the respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally.
10. Appellants - petitioners have stated in the claim petition that the deceased used to work as an auto driver and earn Rs.10,000/- per month, which is also the evidence of PW1.

The learned Tribunal has arrived at a conclusion that the deceased might have been earning BRMR,J Rs.200/-
per day and taken income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month.
Though PW1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for respondent No.2, nothing incriminating is elicited from her.
This Court is of the view that if an amount of Rs.7,000/- per month is fixed towards salary of the deceased which will meet the ends of justice.
The learned Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards future prospects, loss of estate and awarded less amount towards funeral expenses and consortium.
The appellants - petitioners are entitled for the same as per the judgment of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others 1.

13. In the result, MACMA.No.2459 of 2015 is allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced as under:
a) The impugned award dated 30.06.2015, passed in M.V.O.P.No.1045 of 2013,
stands modified.
